units.translation: Codex Aeschylus and Cratinus in the Cretan Women. These notations of the grammarians are perhaps to be understood as meaning that Cratinus said πισσοκωνήτῳ πυρί [with pitch-coned fire], Aeschylus πισσοκωνήτῳ μόρῳ [with pitch-coned doom] for μόρῳ πισσοκωνήτων νεκρῶν [doom of pitch-coned corpses], who are called πισσήρεις [pitched] in the oracle in Athenaeus 12 p. 524a. Γεργίθων τε φόνος πισσήρων τε μόρος [slaughter of the Gergithians and doom of the pitched].
with fire: with the easily kindled; since the things being burned are smeared with pitch

with fire: they smear with pitch, so that it may burn more quickly; and κωνῆσαι [to cone] is to carry around. ετ, κωνῆσαι: to pitch-cone, and to carry around in a circle. And they say πισσοκώνητον μόρον [pitch-coned doom], whenever some people, smeared with pitch, die by fire. Aeschylus in the Cretan Women and Cratinus
